meta.triageRationale: Sized bugfix (ISSUE-6a811b8a, filed 2026-10-04): approval sequencing across the chat host, webview card rendering and the turn lifecycle, with design choices on queueing, deny semantics and grant accumulation for two approval paths.

findings.premise: The design covers every clause of the ISSUE's fix intent: only one request is actionable at a time (only the head is shown and accepted), a follow-up is never cut short by a later approval (one follow-up per batch, run only after the turn ends and every request is decided), deny has a visible effect (rejected chip, follow-up names it as denied, all-denied gives a notice), grants accumulate (grant chain), both paths are handled (turn-ended batch and in-turn decide() relay), there is one outcome row per decision in order, and single-request behaviour is unchanged.
findings.evidence: ISSUE-6a811b8acca60ac5 fixIntent requires: one actionable request at a time; 'a follow-up turn started by an approval is never cancelled by a later approval'; deny with a 'defined, visible effect'; approved grants 'still in force'; both approval paths; outcome chips 'one per decision and in the order'; dir-block and exact-command behaviour unchanged. The LLD covers each one in 2.2/2.3/3.1 and in its edge-case table. The ISSUE's root cause says runTurn calls cancelActive(). That is stale: the current code supersedes through turns.start's newest-message-wins (chat-panel.ts:677-680). The LLD correctly targets the real mechanism. [files: .insrc/artifacts/ISSUE-6a811b8acca60ac5.json, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: Today every approval-request that carries a toolName goes into pendingPerms and is posted at once. Each Approve immediately calls runTurn with only that one tool allowed, and turns.start's newest-message-wins supersedes a running follow-up without killing its process.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:647-659: onEvent posts every event, then `if (ev.kind === 'approval-request' && typeof ev.toolName === 'string' && ev.toolName !== '') pendingPerms.set(...)`. :833/:836 `void runTurn(..., [pending.toolName], { suppressEcho: true })`. turn-lifecycle.ts:221-227 `waitCtl?.abort(); const myGen = ++generation;` and :331-342: a superseded turn keeps being read but reports nothing more ('The previous turn's process is NOT killed'). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts]

findings.premise: In-turn requests usually carry a toolName too, so routing has to use the new resolution field rather than whether a toolName is present.
findings.evidence: cli-adapter.ts:309,318: normalizeApprovalEvent sets toolName from APPROVAL_TOOL_KEYS whenever one is found. chat-panel.ts:653 only tests toolName, so today such an in-turn request is caught by the pendingPerms grant path and never relayed with decide(). Only toolName-less requests reach decide() (test comment at chat-panel.test.ts:1956). The LLD's resolution-based routing correctly fixes this misrouting. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: There are two places where approval-requests are produced: claude's inline system/permission_denied branch (to be marked 'turn-ended') and the shared normalizeApprovalEvent (to be marked 'in-turn'), which serves both claude's control-protocol branch and codex. Marking these two covers every producer.
findings.evidence: Grep finds only two `kind: 'approval-request'` literals in non-test code: cli-adapter.ts:313 (normalizeApprovalEvent) and :538 (the permission_denied branch at :519-546). normalizeApprovalEvent is called at :624 (claude control_request / permission_request / can_use_tool) and :682 (codex approval item). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts]

findings.premise: The host change sites are complete. Besides runTurn's TurnSink, followLiveTurn's FollowSink posts turn-events directly, and the webview bootstrap at chat-panel.ts:514 builds the approval card meta. Both are listed for change, as is postInitialState.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:247-256: followLiveTurn onEvent does `post({ type: 'turn-event', event: ev })`, which would bypass the queue if left alone; the LLD covers it in 2.4. :514 `reg.renderRow({kind:'approval',...,meta:{requestId:ev.requestId,title:ev.title,detail:ev.detail,toolName:ev.toolName}})` has no position/total; the LLD adds them in 2.6/3.2. :258-272 postInitialState re-runs on every 'ready' (:729). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: An approval-request is live-only: it is never written as a transcript row and never replayed on restore. Only permission-outcome rows persist, through recordPermissionOutcome.
findings.evidence: markers.ts:84-86 `case 'approval-request': ... never persisted (k4)` returns null, so appendEvent (chat-panel.ts:708-713) writes no row for it. markers.ts:139 does the same in the webview. chat-panel.ts:214-221: recordPermissionOutcome posts the chip and pushes `{ role: 'permission-outcome', toolName, decision }`. The queue only delays posting and never persists the request, so the invariant holds. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/markers.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: A batch can be ended reliably on the turn's terminal event reaching onEvent: done or error is delivered to sink.onEvent before onTerminal, and an output that ends with no terminal event is turned into an error event.
findings.evidence: turn-lifecycle.ts:343-348: `sink.onEvent(ev); if (isTerminal(ev)) { endTurn(ev, it); sink.onTerminal(ev) }`. :310-321: when the output ends with no done/error, it synthesizes `{ kind: 'error', ..., message: 'the CLI ended without finishing the turn' }` and passes it to onEvent and onTerminal. Superseded, aborted or detached turns return without onTerminal (:292, :309), which the LLD handles explicitly (Stop clears, detach drops, supersede only after a user-typed submit clears). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts]

findings.premise: The existing chat-panel test harness can carry the planned acceptance tests: a fake provider that scripts approval-request events and records decide() calls, so each multi-request test (head-only card, one follow-up per batch, deny, decide-before-next) would fail against today's code.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.test.ts:53 `onDecide?: (turnId, requestId, decision) => void; // S004: decide() relay`. Scripted approval-request events appear at :1581, :1774-2058, including toolName/command/dir-block variants. Today all cards are posted at once (chat-panel.ts:648) and each Approve calls runTurn right away (:833/:836). So 'only the first card is posted', 'turns.start is called once per batch' and 'decide() for the first before the second card' all fail without the fix. Every ac1-ac6 maps to at least one such test. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/chat-panel.test.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

summary.prose: When the assistant asks for several permissions in one turn, the chat now asks for them one at a time. Only the current request has Approve and Deny buttons, shown as "1 of N", and the next appears only once it is decided. For claude, which ends the turn when it is refused, nothing runs until every request from that turn is decided; then one follow-up turn runs with every approved tool allowed and tells the model which actions were approved and which were denied, so no follow-up can cut another short. For providers that wait inside the turn, each decision is passed to the running turn before the next request appears.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Ask for dev-chat approvals one at a time and wait for each decision before proceeding

api.name: approval-request mapping (cli-adapter.ts: claude system/permission_denied branch and normalizeApprovalEvent)
api.signature: normalizeApprovalEvent(turnId: string, raw: Record<string, unknown>): TurnEvent | null  // now sets resolution: 'in-turn'; the permission_denied branch sets resolution: 'turn-ended'

parameters.name: turnId
parameters.purpose: The turn the request belongs to.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.purpose: The provider envelope (control_request / permission_request / can_use_tool / codex approval item).

returns.meaning: An approval-request carrying resolution 'in-turn' (the provider waits for decide()), or null for an idless line as today.

postconditions: claude's system/permission_denied (the turn ends after it) emits resolution: 'turn-ended'.
Every in-turn request (control-protocol can_use_tool, codex approval items) emits resolution: 'in-turn'.
All other fields are unchanged.

api.name: permission-decision (chat-panel handleMessage case)

returns.meaning: The head request is decided: its outcome recorded, and either the next request presented or (batch complete) the follow-up started.

preconditions: A decision is acted on only when requestId is the head of the approval queue; any other requestId (a waiting request, an already-decided one, a stale card) is ignored and logged at debug.
postconditions: Exactly one permission-outcome (live chip + persisted role:'permission-outcome' row) per decided request, in decision order (recordPermissionOutcome, unchanged).

Turn-ended request (resolution 'turn-ended'): the decision is added to the turn's batch; approve of a tool-gate adds its toolName to the session's grant chain; approve of a dir-block posts today's informational message and adds no grant.

In-turn request (resolution 'in-turn', or absent): decide(live.turnId, requestId, decision) is called before the next request is presented. The path is chosen from the event's resolution, never from whether it carries a toolName (in-turn requests usually carry one too).
The next queued request is then posted as the actionable card; if none remain and the originating turn has ended, the batch's follow-up runs (see runTurn).

api.name: runTurn
api.signature: runTurn(text: unknown, allowedTools?: readonly string[], opts?: { readonly suppressEcho?: boolean | undefined }): Promise<void>  // unchanged

parameters.name: text
parameters.purpose: The user's prompt, or the batch follow-up prompt.

parameters.name: allowedTools
parameters.purpose: For a batch follow-up: the session's whole grant chain (every tool approved since the last user-typed turn).

parameters.name: opts.suppressEcho
parameters.purpose: True for the synthetic follow-up (no user bubble), as today.

returns.meaning: The turn ran through turns.start (newest-message-wins, unchanged).

preconditions: A batch follow-up is started only when the originating turn has ended AND every request it raised is decided; at most one follow-up per batch.
postconditions: A user-typed submit (not a follow-up) first clears the approval queue: every still-undecided in-turn request (resolution 'in-turn') whose turn is still live is answered with decide(live.turnId, requestId, 'deny') so the waiting provider process can finish and release the session lease; then each undecided request is recorded as rejected (visible chip) and removed, and the grant chain is reset, so nothing approved earlier silently carries into an unrelated conversation turn.

Follow-up prompt: one approved tool-gate -> today's exact text ('Approved — run exactly this now: <command>' or 'Approved: please proceed with the <tool> action you requested permission for.'); several -> one prompt listing each approved action (exact command where captured) to run now and each denied action not to attempt.
All denied (or only dir-blocks approved): no follow-up turn runs; an informational message says no action was approved.
Requests raised by the follow-up turn form the next batch; the grant chain carries over to it.

api.name: TurnSink.onEvent (runTurn) and FollowSink.onEvent / onEnd (followLiveTurn)
api.signature: TurnSink.onEvent(ev: TurnEvent): void; FollowSink.onEvent(ev: TurnEvent): void; FollowSink.onEnd(): void  // shapes unchanged
postconditions: An approval-request is no longer posted to the webview directly by either sink (runTurn's TurnSink or followLiveTurn's FollowSink after a reload): it is enqueued with its resolution, toolName, command and blockKind, and posted only when it becomes the head.
Every other event is posted and persisted exactly as today; approval-request stays live-only (never a transcript row).
A batch ends when its turn's terminal event (done or error) reaches onEvent, or when a followed turn's onEnd fires; if its requests are all decided, the follow-up starts then.

A turn that ends without a terminal event is handled explicitly: Stop clears the queue (each undecided request recorded as rejected); a chat switch or panel close (detach) drops it without outcome rows; a supersede only happens from a user-typed submit, which clears the queue first.

api.name: approval renderer (render-registry register('approval'))
api.signature: register('approval', (vm: { meta: { requestId: string; title: string; detail?: string; toolName?: string; position?: number; total?: number } }) => Element)

parameters.name: vm.meta.position / vm.meta.total
parameters.purpose: The head's place in the queue, shown as '1 of N' when total > 1.

postconditions: With no position/total (one request) the card renders exactly as today.
The card carries a position label element so its count can be updated in place.

api.name: webview approval handlers (chat-panel.ts bootstrap :514) + HostToWebview
api.signature: HostToWebview |= { type: 'approval-position'; requestId: string; position: number; total: number }

returns.meaning: The existing card is updated in place.

postconditions: The host posts an approval-request card at most once per requestId while it is shown; when requests join the queue behind the head it posts approval-position instead.
The webview finds .insrc-approval[data-request-id=<id>] and rewrites its position label; an unknown id is ignored (never creates a card).

api.name: postInitialState (chat-panel.ts:258, run on every 'ready')

returns.meaning: The full view state is re-sent to a (re)loaded webview.

postconditions: After session-restored, the current queue head (if any) is re-posted as its approval card with position and total, so a webview reloaded on hide/show (no retainContextWhenHidden) shows the actionable request again instead of leaving the queue stuck.

dataModelChanges.details: Host-side, per chat panel, keyed to the active session: an ordered list of undecided requests { requestId, turnId, toolName?, command?, blockKind: 'tool-gate' | 'dir-block', resolution: 'turn-ended' | 'in-turn' }, the current batch { originTurnId, ended: boolean, decisions: { requestId, toolName, command?, blockKind, decision }[] }, and the session's grant chain (Set<string> of approved tool names since the last user-typed turn). Only the head is ever posted to the webview. Cleared (undecided -> rejected) on a user-typed submit; dropped without outcome rows on a session switch or panel close, as undecided live-only cards are today.

+ const approvals = createApprovalQueue()  // { enqueue, head, decide, endTurn, clear, grantChain }

errorCases.scenario: A decision arrives for a requestId that is not the queue head (a waiting request clicked through a stale or second webview, a duplicate click, or a card left over from a previous batch).
errorCases.detection: The permission-decision handler compares msg.requestId with the queue head's requestId before doing anything.
errorCases.response: Ignore it (debug log); no outcome row, no relay, no follow-up. A request that is not in the queue at all still falls through to the live adapter's decide(), which no-ops on an unknown id, as today.
errorCases.userImpact: Nothing happens for the stray click; the actionable card stays the one shown.

errorCases.scenario: The live adapter's decide() throws while relaying a live-turn request (adapter gone, provider unavailable).
errorCases.response: The decision is still recorded as an outcome, the request leaves the queue, and the next request is presented; the failure is logged.
errorCases.userImpact: The chat does not get stuck on an undeliverable decision.

errorCases.scenario: Saving the outcome row fails (session store write error).
errorCases.detection: recordPermissionOutcome saves through trySave, which logs a failing save (existing test at chat-panel.test.ts:2729).
errorCases.response: The live chip is still shown and the queue still advances; the save failure is logged as today.
errorCases.userImpact: The restored session may lack that chip; the run continues.

errorCases.scenario: The originating turn ends with an error after raising some requests.
errorCases.detection: onTerminal receives kind 'error' for the batch's turn.
errorCases.response: The batch is marked ended like a done turn; the user still decides the queued requests and the follow-up runs (or the all-denied notice is shown).
errorCases.userImpact: An errored turn does not strand its approval requests.

edgeCases.input: A turn raises exactly one tool-gate request with a captured command.
edgeCases.expected: One card with no '1 of N'; on Approve the follow-up prompt is exactly 'Approved — run exactly this now: <command>' with allowedTools [tool] (plus earlier grants in the chain); unchanged from today.

edgeCases.input: A turn raises exactly one dir-block request and it is approved.
edgeCases.expected: Today's informational message is posted, an approved chip is recorded, no grant is added and no follow-up runs.

edgeCases.input: Three requests in one turn; the user decides the first before the turn has ended.
edgeCases.expected: The second card is shown after the first is decided; the follow-up waits for both the remaining decisions and the turn's end.

edgeCases.input: All requests in a batch are denied.
edgeCases.expected: One rejected chip per request, no follow-up turn, and an informational message that no action was approved.

edgeCases.input: The user types a new message while requests are still queued.
edgeCases.expected: Undecided in-turn requests are first denied to their live provider with decide(..., 'deny') (so the new turn is not left waiting on a blocked process for the session lease); then each undecided request is recorded as rejected (visible chips) and removed, the grant chain is reset, and the user's message runs as a normal turn.

edgeCases.input: The follow-up turn itself is refused again (raises new requests).
edgeCases.expected: They form the next batch and are asked one at a time; the grant chain from the previous batch is kept and passed with that batch's follow-up.

edgeCases.input: The same tool (e.g. Edit) is approved twice in one batch with different commands.
edgeCases.expected: The grant chain holds the tool once; the follow-up prompt lists both approved actions.

edgeCases.input: A live-turn provider (codex / control protocol) raises two requests in one turn.
edgeCases.expected: Only the first card is shown; its decision is relayed with decide() before the second is shown; no follow-up turn is ever started for live-turn requests.

edgeCases.input: The user switches session or closes the panel with requests queued.
edgeCases.expected: The queue is dropped without outcome rows (the cards were live-only); the other session shows no stray cards.

edgeCases.input: An in-turn provider request that carries a toolName (control-protocol can_use_tool / codex).
edgeCases.expected: Routed by resolution 'in-turn': relayed with decide(), never held for a batch follow-up.

edgeCases.input: The webview reloads (hide/show) while requests are queued.
edgeCases.expected: postInitialState re-posts the head card with its position; deciding it continues the queue.

edgeCases.input: A turn followed after a window reload raises approval requests.
edgeCases.expected: They go through the queue like a live turn's; the followed turn's terminal event or onEnd ends the batch.

edgeCases.input: The user presses Stop with requests queued.
edgeCases.expected: Each undecided request is recorded as rejected and the queue is cleared; no follow-up runs.

edgeCases.input: A fourth request arrives while card 1 of 3 is shown.
edgeCases.expected: No second card; the shown card updates in place to '1 of 4'.

invariantsToPreserve.text: An approval-request is live-only: it is never written to the transcript and never replayed on restore; only decided outcomes persist, as role:'permission-outcome' rows.
Exactly one permission-outcome per decided request, recorded through recordPermissionOutcome, in the order decided.
A dir-block approval never re-runs or grants anything; it posts the informational message.
A synthetic follow-up never echoes a user bubble (suppressEcho).
A decision for an id the host does not hold is relayed to the live adapter's decide(), which no-ops on unknown ids (codex / in-turn relay unchanged).
turns.start keeps newest-message-wins for user-typed turns; the queue only ensures no approval starts a second follow-up while one is running.

Whenever an in-turn request is recorded as rejected while its turn is still live, the provider is told with decide(..., 'deny'): a chip never says rejected while the provider still waits for an answer (turns.start does not kill the previous process; the new turn waits for its lease).

migration.stateBefore: Each approval-request of a turn is recorded in pendingPerms and posted at once as a live card (chat-panel.ts:166, :647-659, :514); every card is actionable; each Approve immediately runs its own follow-up with only that tool allowed, and turns.start's newest-message-wins supersedes a running follow-up (turn-lifecycle.ts:221, :331-333). Live-turn requests are relayed to decide() as clicked.
migration.stateAfter: Approval requests go through a host-side queue: only the head is posted (with '1 of N'), decisions are accepted only for the head, ended-turn batches run one follow-up after the last decision with the accumulated grant chain and a prompt naming approved and denied actions, and live-turn decisions are relayed one at a time. Persisted outcome rows are unchanged in shape and stay one per decision in order.

migrationSteps.action: Add the approval queue module (ordering, head, batch completion, grant chain) with its unit tests; nothing uses it yet.
Mark each approval-request with its resolution in the adapter (permission_denied -> turn-ended; control-protocol / codex -> in-turn).

Route approval-request events through the queue in both runTurn's TurnSink and followLiveTurn's FollowSink, posting only the head; end the batch on the turn's terminal event or the followed turn's onEnd; clear on Stop, drop on detach.

Rewrite the permission-decision handler to act only on the head, record the outcome, relay live-turn decisions, present the next request, and start one follow-up per completed ended-turn batch with the grant chain and the combined prompt (single-request prompts unchanged).

On a user-typed submit, deny every undecided in-turn request to its live provider with decide(..., 'deny'), then record the undecided requests as rejected, clear the queue and reset the grant chain; drop the queue on session switch / panel close.
Add the optional position/total to the approval card meta, the approval-position in-place update message, and re-post the head card from postInitialState on every 'ready'.
Add the multi-request integration tests; keep every existing single-request approval test passing unchanged.

migration.backwardCompat: Internal to the VS Code plugin. Persisted sessions are unchanged: approval-request was never persisted and permission-outcome rows keep their shape, so sessions saved before the change restore exactly as before. The webview message gains only optional fields; a single-request turn behaves byte-for-byte as today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host queue, one serialized follow-up per approval
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The host queues a turn's approval requests, shows only the head, and on each Approve runs a follow-up turn with all grants so far, presenting the next request only after that follow-up ends.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace pendingPerms with an ordered host-side approval queue (requestId, toolName, command?, blockKind, source: ended-turn | live-turn). Only the head is posted to the webview as an actionable card; the others are held host-side and announced as a count ('1 of N'). A decision is accepted only for the head's requestId. On Approve of an ended-turn request the host runs ONE follow-up turn (runTurn) with allowedTools = every tool approved so far in this session, and does not present the next request until that follow-up's onTerminal; requests the follow-up raises are appended to the queue. Deny records a rejected outcome and presents the next request. Live-turn requests are relayed with decide() and the next is presented once the relay returns.
pros: A follow-up is never superseded by a later approval: approvals wait for it
Grants accumulate, so a later follow-up keeps earlier permissions
Works the same for both paths with one queue
cons: N approvals still cost N follow-up turns and N model round-trips
Each follow-up may re-attempt other blocked calls and re-raise requests already queued, producing duplicates the queue must reconcile
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the core sequencing but costs N model round-trips and re-raises requests already in the queue, which weakens fi4 and fi7.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host queue, decide all first, then one combined follow-up
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The host queues the requests and asks them one at a time; once every request from the ended turn is decided it runs a single follow-up turn that pre-allows every approved tool and tells the model which actions were approved and which denied.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same ordered host-side approval queue and head-only presentation as a1, with the decision accepted only for the head. For requests from a turn that ENDED on denial (claude), each decision is recorded (outcome chip, persisted in decision order) and the next request is presented immediately; nothing runs until the queue for that turn is empty. Then exactly one follow-up turn runs with allowedTools = all tools approved so far in the session (accumulated), and a prompt that lists the approved actions (exact commands where captured) to run now and the denied ones not to attempt. If every request was denied, no follow-up runs and a short notice says so. Live-turn requests (codex / control protocol) are relayed one at a time with decide(); the next is presented after the relay. A dir-block approval keeps today's informational response and contributes no grant.
pros: One follow-up per batch: nothing can supersede a follow-up because only one is ever started
No duplicate re-raised requests: the model sees every decision at once
Grants accumulate by construction; deny has a clear effect (that action is named as denied in the follow-up, the others are still asked)
cons: The approved actions run only after the last request is decided, not one by one
Needs a defined behaviour when the user types a new message while requests are still queued

alternativesConsidered.name: Webview gating only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Render every card but enable only the first in the webview, and serialize runTurn calls host-side.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep pendingPerms and the per-approval follow-up. The webview renders all cards but enables buttons only on the oldest undecided one; the host chains each approval's runTurn after the previous follow-up finishes instead of letting turns.start supersede it.
cons: The host still accepts any requestId, so a stale or second window can act out of order
All cards still appear at once, which is the stream the user reported
Grants still do not accumulate; N follow-ups still re-raise requests
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Still shows every card at once (the reported stream), leaves grants un-accumulated and gives deny no defined effect.
